correctness.rationale: For n>=3, the bright span of the nonzero E_lambda|0> reduces both A and the loss projector. On it any eigenvalue z of the lossy Hamiltonian satisfies Im z=-gamma |<0|v>|^2/||v||^2<0: equality would imply an A-eigenvector invisible at 0, impossible in this span. Jordan transients decay for each fixed gamma>0; the dark norm remains constant. The Fourier energies are 2cos(pi k/n)+(-1)^k. For a cross-parity collision the odd double cosine exceeds the even one by 2, so every Galois image of the odd value is nonnegative and of the even value nonpositive. The large cyclotomic field maps onto the relevant subfield automorphisms. For a nonzero one-signed value z+z^-1 of primitive order q the integral norm and AM–GM give absolute mean at least 1, but its mean is 2mu(q)/phi(q). Thus only q=1,2,3,6 can give a nonzero one-signed value; order 4 gives zero. The surviving even/odd pairs are (-1,1) exactly at n=3 mod 6 and (-2,0) exactly at n=2 mod 4; (0,2) would require odd label zero. Modulo the within-parity involution there are n+1 labels, reduced by one in the disjoint exceptional classes. At any energy the trap and antipodal source have projected squared norms (m_e+m_o)/(2n) and overlap (m_e-m_o)/(2n); removing the one-dimensional bright direction leaves 2m_em_o/[n(m_e+m_o)]. This gives the stated two values and zero elsewhere. Replay: RESULT.md lines 32–63. The finite spectral, rational Krylov and dissipative-spectrum verification materials were inspected, not executed; they are not needed for the all-size proof and do not give uniform convergence.
